item.title: Kotlin Coroutines and Structured Concurrency in 2026: A Deep Dive for Android Developers
item.description: I once spent an entire afternoon chasing a bug where a network call kept firing after the user had already backed out of the screen — the response would come back, try to update a ViewModel that no longer had an active observer, and quietly leak. The fix wasn’t a null check or a lifecycle callback. It was realizing I’d launched the coroutine in GlobalScope instead of viewModelScope, which meant nothing was ever going to cancel it.

item.title: Kotlin Multiplatform in 2026: Sharing Code Between Android and iOS Without Compromise
item.description: I’ve shipped the same login screen twice — once in Kotlin for Android, once in Swift for iOS — more times than I’d like to admit. Same validation rules, same API calls, same retry logic, written twice, tested twice, and inevitably drifting apart the moment one platform gets a bugfix the other doesn’t. Kotlin Multiplatform was supposed to fix that, and for a long time it felt like a promising side project more than a real answer.

item.title: Jetpack Compose Goes Compose-First in 2026: What Android Developers Need to Know
item.description: I spent last week migrating a legacy RecyclerView screen to Compose, and about halfway through I realized I wasn’t doing it because I felt like it anymore — I was doing it because Google just told the entire Android ecosystem that Views is no longer where new work happens. That’s a bigger deal than another Compose point release, so I want to walk through what actually changed at I/O 2026, what’s new in Compose 1.

item.title: I built a free Android soundboard that works with an External keyboard
item.description: A few months ago I needed a simple soundboard for a live session. I wanted to trigger audio clips from a Bluetooth keyboard connected to my Android phone - just press a key, hear the sound, instantly. Every app I found was either subscription-based, required an account, or didn’t support physical keyboards at all. So I built CTunes. What CTunes does CTunes maps keyboard keys (A-Z and 0-9) to audio files on your device.

item.title: I Built an Android App Because Android Kept Deleting My Clipboard
item.description: Here’s something that has happened to all of us. You copy a link. Then you copy someone’s phone number. You go to paste the link - and it’s gone. Replaced by the phone number. Android only remembers the last thing you copied. That’s it. One item. Always. I kept running into this. Copying a piece of text, copying something else on top of it, then needing the first thing back with no way to get it.

item.title: Understanding Stateless and Stateful Widgets in Flutter
item.description: Flutter, Google’s UI toolkit, enables developers to build natively compiled applications for mobile, web, and desktop from a single codebase. At the heart of Flutter’s UI framework are widgets, which form the building blocks of any application. In this article, we will explore two fundamental types of widgets in Flutter: Stateless Widgets Stateful Widgets. Watch on YouTube What Are Widgets in Flutter?

item.title: Build Your First Mobile-App in Flutter
item.description: What is Flutter? Flutter is a UI toolkit that is open-source and created by Google, enabling developers to build natively compiled applications for various platforms using a single codebase. It supports building apps for: Mobile: Android and iOS Web: Modern browsers Desktop: Windows, macOS, and Linux Embedded Devices Watch on YouTube Key Features of Flutter Single Codebase: Write one codebase for all platforms.
